subject.title: [Feature]: Make Skill Workshop extensible for custom skill creation workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a core/plugin API or config model that lets custom skill-creation workflows become the authority before `skill_workshop`, or should custom workflows remain ordinary plugin tools/skills that prepare content and then call Skill Workshop?
rationale: The current code already supports plugin tools, tool-call hooks, allowlists, and caller-supplied proposal content, but none of those surfaces defines who owns pre-selection skill-creation authority; choosing that boundary affects product behavior and plugin SDK compatibility.

options.title: Design a narrow authority seam
options.body: Accept the use case and design a generic plugin/tool-policy seam that can route skill-creation requests through a configured custom workflow before final Skill Workshop proposal persistence.

options.title: Keep current routing
options.body: Treat custom workflows as ordinary tools or skills that prepare proposal content and rely on prompting/tool policy, without adding a new authority interface.

options.title: Use a ClawHub convention only
options.body: Encourage publishing custom skill creators as ClawHub plugins or skills and document the convention, but do not add core routing or config surface now.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authority seam
recommendation.body: Accept the use case and design a generic plugin/tool-policy seam that can route skill-creation requests through a configured custom workflow before final Skill Workshop proposal persistence.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the bundled skill-creator surface and recently adjusted the Skill Workshop prompt/tool contract, making him the best evidenced owner for the product-routing choice.
